articles.title: How I made DSQL easier
articles.excerpt: It’s been a year and a half since AWS released Aurora DSQL, a serverless relational database. It’s pay-as-you-go: no paying for idle compute when usage is zero. DynamoDB and DSQL serve different purpo…
articles.body: It’s been a year and a half since AWS released Aurora DSQL, a serverless relational database. It’s pay-as-you-go: no paying for idle compute when usage is zero. DynamoDB and DSQL serve different purposes. I’ve seen it many times, and so have plenty of others: people modelling and using DynamoDB as a relational database. They then complain that they don’t like DynamoDB and that it’s not good, when in reality they just tried to eat soup with a fork and then blamed the fork for their own choices. I was beyond excited to try out DSQL; I enjoyed it. But I never got that out-of-the-box feeling like I did with DynamoDB. I had to do the following manually: Connect to the DSQL cluster with an admin connection. Create your schema and tables. Create a database role.

articles.title: Study: poisoning 0.1% of pretraining data implants a working RCE backdoor in an AI agent
articles.excerpt: 📅 2 November 2026 • arXiv / Hacker News A study posted to arXiv on October 27, 2026 describes a result that changes the threat model for AI agents: poisoning a small share of pretraining data can imp…
articles.body: 📅 2 November 2026 • arXiv / Hacker News A study posted to arXiv on October 27, 2026 describes a result that changes the threat model for AI agents: poisoning a small share of pretraining data can implant a working backdoor in an agent. The paper, numbered 2610.37741 , is authored by Xinyan Hu and 7 co-authors, including Nicholas Carlini, Matthew Jagielski and Javier Rando. The team reports the first demonstration that pretraining-data poisoning can give an agent a remote code execution (RCE) backdoor — code that runs on the machine of the user operating the agent. A CLI agent is a format where the model executes commands on the user's machine, so an implanted code-execution instruction directly touches that machine.

articles.body: Diagram Description The diagram illustrates how to establish a serial communication interface between a computer and a Xiaomi 6 electric scooter controller using an FT232RL USB-to-TTL UART adapter. • The M8 Female Julet Connector (Controller Side): This is the round waterproof connector coming from the scooter's main controller. It exposes 5 specific pins: sw (switch/power), rx (receive data), tx (transmit data), Gnd (ground), and Vcc (power supply). • The FT232RL Circuit (Computer Side): This USB dongle acts as a bridge. It converts the computer's USB signals into serial data that the controller's processor can understand. • The Wire Layout: • Data Lines (Crossed): The rx pin of the Julet connector connects to the tx pin of the FT232RL.

articles.body: This article was written with the help of AI and checked against the site's real code. The test code was run before publishing. A spin wheel looks like a physics toy, but the animation has nothing to do with the result. In the wheel I work on, the winner is chosen first. Then the wheel is told where to stop. That split makes the code simple, and it moves the fairness question to one small function. Here is how that function works, including a change we made because true randomness can look broken. Step 1: Choose the winner without bias The usual snippet is this: const winner = Math . floor ( Math . random () * entries . length ); For a party game this is fine.
